QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_8

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil (SIA) notes that skill-training graduates who were employed at month 6 show only 70% retention at month 24. In SROI terminology, this fade-over-time is captured as:

explanation.text: The Logic: In SROI vocabulary, "drop-off" is the reduction or fade of an outcome over time after the intervention period. It is applied year by year to a multi-year outcome stream to reflect the fact that benefits are rarely permanent. In the scenario, of those employed at month 6, only 70% remain employed at month 24, so 30% of the original outcome has faded by that horizon - this temporal fade is precisely what drop-off captures. The Trap: Deadweight refers to the share of the outcome that would have happened anyway, in the absence of the intervention - it is a counterfactual concept, not a temporal one. Displacement refers to outcomes generated at the expense of another group (substitution), not fade over time. Attribution refers to the share of credit due to other actors/partners. Only drop-off specifically captures the fade-over-time pattern described. Note: The cited workbook pages (146, 157, 158 of the Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook) mention "duration" under the IMP HOW MUCH / CONTRIBUTION dimensions and list drop-off risk as an IMP risk factor, but they do not, in the pages checked, define drop-off specifically as "SROI fade-over-time" in the way used in this question. The framing above reflects general SROI methodology as practised in social-impact evaluation.
